GIC-Based Variable Selection Using Boltzmann Machine

Source: R/GICSelection_Boltzmann.R
GICSelectionBoltzmann.Rd

Performs variable selection using the Generalized Information Criterion ('GIC') combined with a Boltzmann-like simulated annealing approach. The optimization logic is implemented in 'Julia' and accessed from 'R' through the 'JuliaCall' interface.

Usage

GICSelectionBoltzmann(
  X,
  Y,
  Init_Columns,
  Calculate_GIC,
  Calculate_GIC_short,
  T = 0.1,
  Nsim = 5,
  k = NULL,
  gamma = 0.6
)

Arguments

X

A numeric design matrix with n rows (observations) and p columns (predictors).

Y

A numeric response vector (length n) or an n x q matrix.

Init_Columns

Integer vector of indices specifying the initial set of predictors.

Calculate_GIC

Character string giving the name of the 'Julia' function to compute full GIC values.

Calculate_GIC_short

Character string giving the name of the 'Julia' function to compute approximate GIC values.

T

Numeric scalar. The temperature parameter controlling stochasticity in the simulated annealing process (default: 0.1).

Nsim

Integer. Number of passes over the (once-shuffled) variables (default: 5).

k

Optional integer model-size cap, as in GICSelection(); NULL (default) means no cap.

gamma

EBIC tuning constant (default 0.6); ignored by other criteria.

Value

A list with the following components:

GIC_list

List of GIC values returned for each run.

GIC_coeff

Indices of the variables selected in the final run.

Details

This method uses temperature-based control to introduce stochasticity in model exploration. It supports custom GIC formulations by passing the names of 'Julia' functions and works with both univariate and multivariate responses.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (requireNamespace("JuliaCall", quietly = TRUE)) {
  julia_available <- FALSE
  tryCatch({
    JuliaCall::julia_setup(installJulia = FALSE)
    julia_available <- TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Julia not available: ", e$message)
  })

  if (julia_available) {
    set.seed(123)
    n <- 100; p <- 10; k <- 3
    X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)
    beta <- c(rep(1.5, k), rep(0, p - k))
    Y <- X %*% beta + rnorm(n)

    result <- GICSelectionBoltzmann(
      X = X,
      Y = Y,
      Init_Columns = 1:p,
      Calculate_GIC = "Calculate_SIC",
      Calculate_GIC_short = "Calculate_SIC_short",
      Nsim = 3
    )
    print(result$GIC_coeff)
  }
}
} # }
